‘Clayface’ In Staring Contest With Elizabeth Holmes & Nathan Fielder For No. 1 Over Sluggish Halloween Weekend – Sunday AM Update
2026 Worldwide Box Office Headed To Near $36B, Best Since 2019
‘The Further Mis-Adventures Of Cliff Booth’: Netflix Brad Pitt Pic Won’t Be Playing Top Chains Regal & Cinemark
SUNDAY AM: Warner Bros’ Clayface with all his trick-or-treat attitude thinks he’s No. 1 for the weekend with $10.4M , however, A24’s You Can See Everything is reporting $10.6M .
Clayface won Halloween with $4.2M while Nathan Fielder and Elizabeth Holmes’ collected $3.58M from moviegoers. Sunday looks to belong to the duo with $3.45M. Clayface is looking at $2.8M today, and we hear You Can See Everything is already ahead of the DC pic in its hourlies.
A source remarked that You Can See Everything is always ahead in the hourlies as its older female audience buys advance tickets. You Can See Everything was ahead in hourlies last weekend against Clayface and the James Watkins directed movie still won. Some rivals show Clayface with the overall 3-day edge for No. 1, with a $200K to half million gap ahead of You Can See Everything. The fight will continue into tomorrow AM.
All pics grossed an estimated $62.2M, -38% from last weekend, and, oy, the third lowest grossing weekend of the year ahead of Jan. 23-25 ($54.7M) and Feb. 6-8 ($61.9M, when Send Help opened). Next year, Halloween falls on a Sunday which is better, but still not overall great for business. Watch on Deadline
Clayface is No. 1 worldwide with $22.8M and an $83M running cume. You Can See Everything is only open in Turkey at 120 locations (wide for the market) and hits Australia/NZ on Nov. 12 with UK on Nov. 20, so no big grosses yet.
Netflix opened Peter Berg’s WWII movie The Mosquito Bowl in 349 locations to $455K with a per theater of $1,3K. We’re hearing that results were flat. Look, this is going to happen with some Netflix limited releases. Grosses won’t always be dazzling, and it also depends on how much marketing heft they devote to a theatrical push in weekend one, not to mention the wider they go, the bigger the gross (duh). It will be interesting to see the pop that The Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth gets in AMC Imax during its Thankgiving run. In regards to Regal and Cinemark, they’ll be playing Lionsgate’s The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping in Imax over the holiday.

SATURDAY AM: Both A24’s You Can See Everything and Warner Bros/DC’s Clayface remain above $10M in what isn’t the worst weekend this year at the domestic box office, but close with all titles grossing north of $63M.
However, sources believe Elizabeth Holmes and Nathan Fielder are more alluring than a DC complex character whose face is melting, hence the 3 hour documentary has the edge, and also a shot at $11M . Meanwhile, A24 is celebrating that they’re crossing the half billion mark at the domestic B.O. YTD, their highest ever.
Exits for Clayface remain strong on Screen Engine/Rentrak’s PostTrak with 68% definite recommend and 4 1/2 stars and an 85% positive with guys leading the way at 63%. Given that it’s the third week of You Can See Everything, its exits are no longer tracking on PostTrak.
It’s set to rain in LA tonight. Typically in this market, folks stay off the road, but we’ll see if they take shelter in cinemas. The worst weekend of 2026 belongs to Jan. 23-25 ($54.8M) when the Amazon MGM Studios’ sci-fi title Mercy starring Chris Pratt opened.

FRIDAY PM UPDATE: Halloween’s trick on the weekend domestic box office is currently seeing a fight between A24’s You Can See Everything and Warner Bros/DC’s Clayface with $10M+ apiece, though the odds are in favor the incarcerated failed Theranos founder versus a Gotham celebrity whose face melts.
You Can See Everything is counting $3.2M today for a $10M-$11M third weekend take, while Clayface is eyeing $3.1M and a $10M+ second frame. By Sunday, that would take the running cume for the Lance Oppenheim and Nathan Fielder documentary to $63.7M on the high end and the James Watkins-directed DC movie to $43.7M .

Fourth is Black Bear’s second weekend of R-rated femme sex comedy Wicker , which could see a post-Halloween boost on Sunday from female audiences. Second Friday is $1.2M, and the second weekend is around $3.5M at 2,374, for a -39% hold and a running total of $12.7M.
Fifth is Paramount/Legendary’s third weekend of Street Fighter at 2,825 sites for a $1M third Friday and $3.3M third weekend, -61% for a running total by Sunday of $53.1M .
PREVIOUS FRIDAY AM: Fueled by nonstop memes on social, not to mention, Elizabeth Holmes and Nathan Fielder being the “it” Halloween costumes, A24’s You Can See Everything is destined to lead the sluggish holiday frame with around $10M+ , we hear.
Far and away, the three-hour documentary co-directed by Lance Oppenheim is the sales leader, we understand as of today; the pic expected to ease by around 40% from its second-weekend take of $19.5M.
You Can See Everything ends its second week with $27.1M and a 14-day cume of $52.7M vs. Warner Bros/DC’s Clayface , which ends its first week with $33.6M . That James Watkins-directed Batman villain spinoff is hoping to ease by 60% in its second weekend, which is on the high end for a genre movie.
While Michael Moore’s Fahreinheit 9/11 is the highest-grossing non-nature, non-concert documentary with $119.1M domestic, docs that You Can See Everything already has surpassed stateside include Moore’s Bowling for Columbine ($21.5M, 2022), Al Gore’s An Inconvenient Truth ($24.1M, 2006) and the Leonardo DiCaprio-narrated Hubble 3D ($52.5M, 2010).
With rain expected in B.O. capital Los Angeles on Saturday and the buzz still hot on You Can See Everything, will moviegoers take three hours out of their festivities to see this movie? Typically, horror movies, like Clayface, lead on Halloween, but we’re dealing with an anomaly here.

Similar to last year, Halloween is landing on the weekend, and that spells doom for the box office. Last year, the holiday fell on a Friday with all pics grossing $57.3M over Friday-Sunday (the fifth-lowest-grossing weekend of 2025). The previous times Halloween fell on a Saturday were Covid 2020 (when a majority of theaters were closed) and 2015 ( The Martian led the weekend with a $11.7M fifth frame, and the overall weekend grossed $74.1M). Some box office sources argue that the weekend might not get sucker-punched as bad as we think: Unlike Super Bowl weekend, moviegoers still can make it to matinees Saturday or attend tonight.

Nonetheless, it’s not a time for the major studios to waste their time or money on opening a wide release. The most notable wide release this weekend is Briarcliff Entertainment’s Kevin Lewis-directed indie holiday slasher Christmas at the Kringles at 1,825 theaters. The pic brought in $200K in previews last night and is expected to do in the low single digits over the weekend. Blurb for the movie starring Ron Livingston, Rob Riggle, Rachel Bilson and Tom Lennon: The Severson family moves to a suburban neighborhood where their neighbors, the Kringles, celebrate Christmas year-round and harbor sinister intentions to hypnotize and indoctrinate them. Rotten Tomatoes critical score is gulp, 0%.

Also, going wider is Black Bear’s critically acclaimed female pleaser Wicker, from 1,471 sites to an estimated 2,374 locations.
